summary: A write-up of the TELNET command at Host LL for the CP/CMS time-sharing system, which could run in half or full duplex and with ASCII or EBCDIC codes. It describes keyboard conventions for IBM 2741 terminals and local control commands, including reading input from a file. The text says it was not reviewed for public release.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC documents the TELNET command on Host LL. It explains how the command handled terminal input, two character codes, and local control commands.

subtitle: How Host LL's CP/CMS TELNET command supported remote terminals.

tldr.problem: Users on Host LL needed to access terminal-oriented systems over the ARPA Network using CP/CMS and an IBM 2741 keyboard.
tldr.mechanism: The local TELNET command supports half- or full-duplex operation, ASCII or EBCDIC, keyboard control conventions, and file input and output commands.
tldr.outcome: The RFC documents one Host LL implementation and says its material was not reviewed for public release.

sections.title: TELNET at Host LL
sections.content:
RFC 452 documents a TELNET command for use with the CP/CMS time-sharing system at Host LL. It allows users to access terminal-oriented systems on the ARPA Network and supports both half-duplex and full-duplex modes.

The document says it was intended for ARPA Network use and had not been reviewed for public release.
sections.plainLanguage: The TELNET command lets a Host LL user connect to a terminal-based system elsewhere on the network. This document describes that local version of the command.

sections.title: Terminal Modes and Character Codes
sections.content:
Users can choose ASCII or EBCDIC; ASCII is the default. Full-duplex operation is also the default, with the keyboard available for input, while half-duplex operation locks and unlocks the keyboard according to the received output and selected mode.

The RFC explains how a control character followed by another key enters codes that are not present on the IBM 2741 keyboard. It also provides mappings between ASCII, EBCDIC, and TELNET control codes.
sections.plainLanguage: The command can translate between network ASCII and EBCDIC, a code used by the IBM system. A control-key convention lets users enter codes their keyboard lacks.

sections.title: Local Control Commands
sections.content:
A line beginning with the control character and a space starts a local TELNET control command. The documented commands can change the control character or mode, send TELNET controls, direct input from a file, and direct output to a file.

The RFC calls the file features a rudimentary file-transfer facility. It also documents commands for RJS reader, printer, and punch use.
sections.plainLanguage: Special commands can route input from a file or save output to one. Other commands change the mode or send a TELNET control code.
